publisher: Deloitte (Deloitte Consulting LLP, Office of the CTO)
title: Tech Trends 2025
notes: 16th annual edition ('our 16th trip around the sun'). Six trends, each in Now / New / Next sections; 'New' sections carry the 18-to-24-month horizon, 'Next' sections the next decade. The introduction ('AI everywhere') and conclusion ('Breadth is the new depth') are not trends. Edition-level claim: AI 'will be as foundational as electricity to daily business and personal lives'. published from the edition page's publishDate; the PDF file on deloitte.com was regenerated in February 2026.

entries.label: Spatial computing takes center stage
entries.quote: In the coming years, advancements in AI could lead to seamless spatial computing experiences and improved interoperability, ultimately enabling AI agents to anticipate and proactively meet users’ needs.
entries.subject: Spatial computing

entries.label: What’s next for AI?
entries.quote: Over the next 18 to 24 months, key AI vendors and enterprise users are likely to have a toolkit of models comprising increasingly sophisticated, robust LLMs along with other models more applicable to day-to-day use cases.
entries.subject: AI models (LLMs, small language models, agentic AI)
entries.horizon: next 18 to 24 months; next decade (agentic AI)
entries.note: 'Next: There’s an agent for that' section: 'In the next decade, AI could be wholly focused on execution instead of human augmentation.'

entries.label: Hardware is eating the world
entries.quote: we anticipate that enterprises will be grappling with decisions about the first two areas over the next 18 to 24 months.
entries.subject: AI hardware (AI chips, AI PCs, edge devices, data centers)
entries.horizon: next 18 to 24 months; robotics: next decade
entries.note: 'The first two areas' are AI-embedded devices and the Internet of Things, and data centers. Same chapter: 'Over the next decade, advancements in robotics applied to more and more complex situations could revolutionize the nature of manufacturing and other physical labor.'

entries.label: IT, amplified: AI elevates the reach (and remit) of the tech function
entries.quote: Deloitte’s foresight analysis suggests that, by 2027, even in the most conservative scenario, gen AI will be embedded into every company’s digital product or software footprint
entries.subject: Generative AI in the IT function
entries.horizon: next 18 to 24 months; next decade (new lean IT)
entries.note: Same section: 'Over the next 18 to 24 months, the nature of the IT function is likely to change as enterprises increasingly employ generative AI.' Executive summary uses the title 'IT, amplified: AI elevates the reach (and remit) of tech talent'.

entries.label: Quantum computing and cybersecurity: A post-quantum cryptography migration guide for leaders
entries.quote: Experts predict that quantum computers, which could mature within five to 20 years, will have significant implications for cybersecurity because of their ability to break existing encryption methods and digital signatures.
entries.subject: Post-quantum cryptography
entries.horizon: five to 20 years (quantum computer maturity, attributed to experts)
entries.note: Executive summary and figure 1 title the trend 'The new math: Solving cryptography in an age of quantum'; the table of contents uses the label recorded here. The horizon is attributed to 'experts', not stated as Deloitte's own.

entries.label: The intelligent core: AI changes everything for core modernization
entries.quote: Core systems providers have invested heavily in AI, rebuilding their offerings and capabilities around an AI-fueled or AI-first model.
entries.subject: AI in core enterprise systems (ERP)
entries.note: Executive summary quote. No chapter-level horizon sentence found.
